library_preparation_preflight.summary: libfreenect2 binds a USB Kinect v2 driver; no physical device exists in CI, so tests must target the hardware-independent API surface instead of real device I/O. No extra Maven dependency or Docker image is needed beyond the standard org.bytedeco:libfreenect2(-platform) scaffold.
library_preparation_preflight.agent_guidance: Freenect2.enumerateDevices()/openDefaultDevice() will see zero devices in CI (no physical Kinect v2 USB hardware is attached or emulatable) — write tests that assert graceful zero-device behavior rather than attempting real frame capture. For meaningful coverage, exercise the hardware-independent surface: Frame allocation and pixel/byte-buffer access, Logger subclassing and global logger registration, Registration built from synthetic IrCameraParams/ColorCameraParams (test undistortDepth/apply/getPointXYZ with fabricated depth+color Frame data), and PacketPipeline construction via CpuPacketPipeline (avoids any GPU/display dependency the OpenGL pipeline would pull in). If a native-image run ever fails with UnsatisfiedLinkError mentioning libX11/libXrandr/libXinerama/libXxf86vm/libXcursor, that's a missing system X11 library on the runner (pulled in dynamically by GLFW) rather than a metadata or test defect — ubuntu-22.04 GitHub-hosted runners normally have these preinstalled.
risks: Full functional coverage (actual depth/color/IR frame capture from a real sensor) is unreachable in CI since no Kinect v2 hardware is present or emulatable via Docker; expect metadata coverage to plateau on classes that don't require an open device handle.

The bundled native library dynamically links system X11 libraries on Linux (via statically-linked GLFW); an unusually minimal container or runner image lacking libX11/libXrandr/libXinerama/libXxf86vm/libXcursor could fail to load the native library even for CPU-pipeline-only usage.
